fragments.body:
The Eyelid is a big white three-story Victorian just beyond the railroad tracks, and its breakfasts are the stuff of county legend — biscuits like clouds, gravy with intent, coffee that tastes like a decision. The menu has never changed. No grocery truck has ever been seen making a delivery. The kitchen door is always closed, and from behind it comes a sound like someone humming in two voices at once.

Guests are advised not to ask. The one man who did — a traveling salesman, 1988 — was served an extra biscuit and found himself unable to remember the question.
fragments.thread: The old well out back is older than the house. Anna d'Konda says it smells like watermelon down there. Nobody has asked her how she knows.
fragments.title: Breakfast

fragments.body:
There are nine rooms at the Eyelid. Eight of them rent. Room #6 has not been rented since 1974, according to the register — but the bed is always made, the lamp is always warm, and guests in Room #5 report a measured pacing overhead at exactly 3 a.m.

The door stands slightly ajar. It has stood slightly ajar for fifty years. Everyone who has ever stayed at the Eyelid has tried it, and it has never once opened further.
fragments.thread: Go on. Try it. Everyone does.
fragments.title: Room #6

name: The Eyelid Boarding House
tagline: Three stories. Legendary breakfasts. One locked mystery.
